<a id="entry-bring-the-ontology-kit-source-onto-main"></a>

## Entry 1 — 2026-09-08 — Bring the Ontology Kit source onto main

*Kind: product. Status: accepted.*

## Context

`main` had governance and agent-instruction scaffolding installed (Project Narrative) but no
product code yet; the actual Ontology Kit implementation existed only on a branch whose history no
longer connected to `main`, so a normal PR/merge wasn't possible (GitHub refuses a PR between
branches with no common history).

## Decision

Rather than force-pushing over either branch's history, created a new branch from `main` and
copied the kit's tree onto it file by file, checking each path for a collision first. Only one
file (`README.md`) existed on both sides, and it was already identical, so nothing needed
reconciling by hand.

## Consequences

`main` now contains the full kit: installer, linter, templates, skill, and test suite, alongside
the existing Project Narrative scaffold. `feat/ontology-kit` (the orphaned branch) is left in
place, unmerged, for reference. No shared history exists between it and `main`; future work should
branch from `main` going forward.

<a id="entry-add-codeowners-naming-the-repository-owner"></a>

## Entry 2 — 2026-09-08 — Add CODEOWNERS naming the repository owner

*Kind: product. Status: accepted.*

## Context

`main` had no branch protection and no CODEOWNERS, so any push could land directly with no review.
The repository is moving to a required-review model for `main`.

## Decision

Added a single catch-all CODEOWNERS entry (`* @jamiemitchellconsultants`) rather than per-path
ownership, since there is currently one maintainer. Branch protection (required PR review, required
code-owner review, admin override allowed) is applied separately via the GitHub API/UI, not in this
PR, since it's a repository setting rather than repository content.

## Consequences

Once branch protection is enabled, pull requests into `main` will require review before merging,
except that repository admins can override the requirement. Future maintainers or path-specific
owners can be added to CODEOWNERS by extending this file with more specific patterns above the
catch-all line.

<a id="entry-design-and-plan-owl-ttl-machine-readable-ontology"></a>

## Entry 3 — 2026-09-08 — Design and plan: OWL/TTL machine-readable ontology

*Kind: product. Status: accepted.*

## Context

The kit's ontology was Markdown-only: easy for humans and agents to read and diff, but nothing
about it was machine-readable, and it was hand-maintained — exactly the two-representations-drift
problem the rest of the kit exists to close for domain vocabulary generally.

## Decision

`ontology.ttl` becomes the authoritative file; `ontology.md` becomes generated output, regenerated
by a new `build-ontology.mjs` (migrate once if no `.ttl` exists, then always render), enforced by a
new CI staleness check. A small kit-owned OWL vocabulary (`kit:` namespace) gives every ontology
section a formal type. Considered and rejected: hand-maintaining both files with a drift check
instead of generation (more flexible, but drift-prone); shipping Narrative's own files as kit
templates (rejected — Narrative is a separate tool this kit doesn't own, so the spec recommends it
but only scaffolds on explicit agreement, using this repository's own files as the worked example).

## Consequences

Editing the ontology moves from `ontology.md` to `ontology.ttl`; the `.md` becomes a reviewable,
generated artifact, similar to `Narrative.md`. A new `docs/ai-agent-install.md` becomes the primary
onboarding path for an AI agent given a short "add the ontology kit" prompt. The `kit:` vocabulary
is now a design commitment — widening it later is a breaking change to the parser/renderer, not a
docs update. Implementation is not yet started; this PR is spec and plan only.

<a id="entry-implement-owl-ttl-machine-readable-ontology"></a>

## Entry 4 — 2026-09-08 — Implement OWL/TTL machine-readable ontology

*Kind: product. Status: accepted.*

## Context

PR #6 merged the approved spec and implementation plan making `ontology.ttl` the authoritative ontology source with `ontology.md` generated from it. The kit was still Markdown-only: nothing machine-readable, and the `.md` hand-maintained. This PR is the implementation of that plan (all ten tasks), verified by `npm test` (243 pass) plus an end-to-end install-migrate-check run in a scratch repo.

## Decision

Implemented the plan as written, with two corrections discovered during implementation where the plan contradicted itself: (1) `modelToTriples` emits `kit:invariant` triples inline with their concept's class triples rather than in a trailing loop, because subject-grouped Turtle serialization otherwise breaks the specified `parse(serialize(x)) === x` round trip; (2) the plan's entity-triple test expectation was updated to include the invariant annotation the spec mandates on the same subject. Also registered the new `NAMESPACE_URI`/`ONTOLOGY_TTL_PATH` placeholders in `tests/templates.test.mjs` and refreshed README's installed-file list, which the plan left stale. Rejected alternative: weakening the round-trip tests to order-insensitive comparison — kept them exact and fixed the implementation instead.

## Consequences

Adopting repositories edit `ontology.ttl` and regenerate `ontology.md` via `node scripts/build-ontology.mjs`; CI fails on a stale `.md` before the term check runs. The shipped example `ontology.md` lost its section guidance prose (it cannot round-trip through TTL) — that material now lives only in the skill references. The `kit:` vocabulary is now a design commitment: widening it later breaks the parser/renderer pair. `ontology-setup` is a Claude Code skill, so generic agents use the new `docs/ai-agent-install.md` runbook instead.

<a id="entry-chore-dogfood-the-ontology-kit-on-its-own-repository"></a>

## Entry 5 — 2026-09-08 — chore: dogfood the ontology kit on its own repository

*Kind: product. Status: accepted.*

## Context

The kit installs a vocabulary discipline into other repositories but had never run it against itself. Its own docs (`README.md`, `docs/how-it-works.md`, the `ontology-setup` skill's reference guides) already carry real domain vocabulary — `Installer`, `TargetRepository`, `OntologyConfig`, `Ownership`, and so on — with no mechanism keeping it from drifting the same way the kit warns adopters it will.

## Decision

Installed the kit into its own repository rather than leaving it undogfooded, and seeded the ontology from the kit's real code and docs rather than filling in the template's placeholder rows. Excluded `templates/` and `docs/superpowers/` from the check via `ignorePaths` instead of trying to make their contents (deliberately generic example terms meant for adopters, and an archived planning transcript full of test fixtures) pass as real domain vocabulary — forcing either into the ontology would have been decoration, not discipline.

## Consequences

This repository is now bound by its own protocol: any future change to the installer, the config shape, or the kit's own vocabulary must update `docs/ontology.md` in the same commit, and CI enforces it via `.github/workflows/ontology-lint.yml`. The allowlist currently holds 14 entries, all illustrative placeholders in reference docs rather than real drift — worth revisiting if that ratio grows as the kit's own documentation expands.

<a id="entry-docs-feature-accept-semantic-ontology-matching-vision"></a>

## Entry 7 — 2026-10-30 — docs(feature): accept semantic ontology matching vision

*Kind: product. Status: accepted.*

## Context

The kit's current semantic reviewer is optional, advisory, and examines only added lines. The feature discussion established a different product need: trusted collaborators' PRs should be checked for semantic mismatches across each changed Markdown file, with a path for agents to resolve findings and maintainers to dismiss false positives.

## Decision

Accept the vision in `docs/features/semantic-ontology-matching/01-vision.md`: findings block merge; model or configuration failure is reported as not reviewed and does not block; repository maintainers own model configuration and credentials; the PR author's agent may commit corrections under the author's identity, while other agents propose them; a maintainer may dismiss a specific false positive with a recorded reason. The pilot has no numerical value target and may be disabled if maintainers see no subjective value.

## Consequences

The analyst and architect phases must define the exact review, resolution, and secure execution behavior. This PR records product intent; it does not yet change the existing reviewer or its advisory documentation. Fork PRs remain outside this feature and have a separate manual-investigation issue (#21).

<a id="entry-docs-feature-define-semantic-matching-behaviours"></a>

## Entry 8 — 2026-10-30 — docs(feature): define semantic matching behaviours

*Kind: product. Status: accepted.*

## Context

The accepted vision in #14 and PR #22 calls for blocking semantic findings on trusted collaborators' same-repository PRs. The existing optional reviewer is advisory and examines added lines only. The analyst phase had to make the check's observable behavior explicit, including outage, partial review, correction, and dismissal cases.

## Decision

Accept B1–B14 in `docs/features/semantic-ontology-matching/02-behaviours.md`. Review the full current contents of changed eligible Markdown files against the PR's proposed ontology. An active finding blocks merge; the author's agent may correct the branch under the author's identity, while another agent proposes a correction. A maintainer may dismiss a specific finding with a recorded reason for the current revision. The latest run controls the check, so an unavailable or unusable model permits merge with an explicit not-reviewed notice, even after an earlier blocking finding. A partial run blocks if it returned a finding; otherwise it permits merge with incomplete-coverage notice. Repository maintainers control model configuration and credentials. Fork PRs remain outside the automated scope under #21.

## Consequences

The architect must design trusted execution, model configuration, run and dismissal persistence, and PR-visible findings and notices around these behaviors. The outage policy intentionally allows a later failed run to clear an earlier semantic block; the prior finding stays visible as history. The deterministic term check remains independent. This PR introduces behavior and vocabulary only; it does not turn on a semantic check.

Verification: ontology term check passed (60 files, 27 terms); `npm test` passed (243 tests).

AI-Fingerprint: sha256:9a0a869685df

<a id="entry-docs-feature-define-semantic-review-architecture"></a>

## Entry 9 — 2026-10-30 — docs(feature): define semantic review architecture

*Kind: product. Status: accepted.*

## Context

The accepted behaviours in PR #25 require a semantic finding to block a trusted collaborator's PR, while an unavailable later run permits merge and reports that review did not run. The reviewer needs model credentials, author-supplied Markdown as input, durable findings and dismissals, and a PR status that branch protection can require. The kit's existing advisory reviewer runs from the PR checkout and remains an optional separate path during the pilot.

## Decision

Use a secretless PR trigger followed by trusted default-branch code in a `workflow_run` worker. Read model settings from the default branch's `OntologyConfig` and use a default-branch-only Actions environment secret. Fetch PR contents as data, review all changed eligible Markdown in bounded requests, and validate grounded findings. Publish the latest result in a fixed required commit-status context, keeping each run and each reasoned dismissal visible in PR comments. Ship the blocking path as a separate opt-in so existing advisory installations do not become blocking on upgrade.

These decisions are recorded in [ADR 0001 — trusted workflow](https://github.com/jamiemitchellconsultants/InternalOntology/blob/feature/semantic-ontology-matching/architect/docs/adr/0001-trusted-semantic-review-workflow.md), [ADR 0002 — outcome status](https://github.com/jamiemitchellconsultants/InternalOntology/blob/feature/semantic-ontology-matching/architect/docs/adr/0002-semantic-outcome-status.md), [ADR 0003 — PR ledger](https://github.com/jamiemitchellconsultants/InternalOntology/blob/feature/semantic-ontology-matching/architect/docs/adr/0003-semantic-review-pr-ledger.md), and [ADR 0004 — opt-in rollout](https://github.com/jamiemitchellconsultants/InternalOntology/blob/feature/semantic-ontology-matching/architect/docs/adr/0004-semantic-review-opt-in.md).

## Consequences

The developer must implement and test both workflow halves, PR data validation, full-file coverage, status publication on the evaluated commit, and revision-scoped dismissal processing. Maintainers must configure the protected environment and require the fixed status context. A later unavailable run intentionally supersedes an earlier block while retaining its finding comment as history. Fork PR workflow approval and manual investigation remain tracked in #21. The deterministic `TermChecker` stays independent.

Verification: ontology term check passed (66 files, 31 terms); `npm test` passed (243 tests).

## Entry 10 — 2026-10-30 — docs(feature): plan semantic matching implementation

*Kind: product. Status: accepted.*

## Context

PR #27 accepted a trusted follow-up workflow, complete changed-file review, commit-status outcomes, PR-visible finding and dismissal records, and a separate opt-in from the existing advisory reviewer. The developer phase now needs a test-first sequence that another agent can execute without re-deciding that structure.

## Decision

Implement the feature in eight independently testable, individually committed tasks: strict configuration; GitHub PR input and eligibility; lossless file batching; grounded model assessment; run ledger and status publication; maintainer dismissals; trusted workflow orchestration; and opt-in installation with runbook and end-to-end proof. The detailed plan pins interfaces, fixtures, exact files, and failure outcomes. Every task runs the ontology check and `npm test` before its commit. The accepted architecture and ADRs remain the design authority.

## Consequences

The build can proceed one task and one commit at a time after this plan is reviewed and merged. It must preserve the byte-identical installed-script rule, keep PR data out of secret-bearing execution, and verify the required status on the evaluated GitHub commit in a disposable repository. No implementation code is introduced by this PR. If live branch-protection behavior cannot be verified, the build PR must state that limitation for acceptance rather than claim it passed.

Verification: ontology term check passed (68 files, 31 terms); `npm test` passed (243 tests).

<a id="entry-feat-add-opt-in-semantic-ontology-matching-pilot"></a>

## Entry 11 — 2026-10-30 — feat: add opt-in semantic ontology matching pilot

*Kind: product. Status: accepted.*

## Context

The accepted vision, behaviours, architecture, and plan in PRs #22, #25, #27, and #29 require blocking findings for trusted same-repository collaborators, while an unavailable later run must allow the PR to proceed with a visible notification. The reviewer must treat PR files as data and keep model credentials in a protected default-branch environment. The final independent review also found that reflected ledger markers and an identification-job race could wrongly clear a finding.

## Decision

Ship semantic matching as a separate opt-in. The secretless trigger launches trusted default-branch code; read-only identification selects PRs, and per-PR serialized review and finalization publish the latest outcome on the current head and verified test-merge SHA. Validate model findings against exact file passages and ontology evidence; retain findings and reasoned maintainer dismissals in PR comments. Parse only the publisher-owned ledger marker at the end of each comment and escape reflected marker syntax. Only trusted same-repository collaborators enter the model review path.

## Consequences

Maintainers configure the model endpoint and a protected `ONTOLOGY_SEMANTIC_LLM_API_KEY` environment secret, then require `ontology/semantic-match` from GitHub Actions. An active finding blocks merge; dismissal or a later unavailable result updates the status while preserving earlier comments. Fork PRs remain a manual-investigation follow-up in #21. The feature remains disabled by default pending subjective value in the pilot.

Verification: `npm test` passed (303/303); ontology term check passed (69 files, 31 terms); `actionlint` passed all three new workflows. In a [disposable trial PR](https://github.com/jamiemitchellconsultants/ontology-semantic-trial-20261030/pull/1), the [updated trusted workflow](https://github.com/jamiemitchellconsultants/ontology-semantic-trial-20261030/actions/runs/41085701941) completed identification, review, and finalization, publishing a successful unavailable status under branch protection because no model credential was installed. Earlier trial runs verified no-eligible status; a manually simulated failure status blocked merge and a later unavailable status unblocked it. An actual hosted model finding still needs acceptance with a configured pilot model. An empty changed Markdown blob currently reports incomplete coverage rather than a reviewed empty file; this does not clear a finding.

<a id="entry-docs-feature-vision-for-source-knowledge-graph"></a>

## Entry 13 — 2026-11-02 — docs(feature): vision for source knowledge graph

*Kind: product. Status: accepted.*

## Context

The current Kit gives agents a canonical vocabulary, while repository structure, dependencies, tests, and deployment facts remain scattered. A JointBooking Graphify spike showed useful file-and-line evidence but also an inferred path through test helpers. The target is a wider graph for agent grounding, with C4 diagrams as one downstream view. Corporate use requires a high bar for external dependencies.

## Decision

The product-owner vision makes agent grounding the primary outcome. An agent prepares a source-owned graph before a pull request; deterministic CI checks its structure and evidence, and maintainers review meaning. Repositories may declare partial coverage. Evaluation spans C#, TypeScript, Java, and Python. The JointBooking pilot considers Terraform alone for deployment evidence. Graphify remains a research aid and is not a Kit or CI dependency.

## Consequences

The analyst can define the observable behavior and coverage rules without assuming one graph schema or extraction method. The architect must preserve byte-identical installed scripts and repository-specific configuration. Division-ontology can later consume reviewed source facts at recorded commits and derive C4 views where evidence is available. Numeric grounding targets wait for a representative baseline.

<a id="entry-docs-feature-behaviours-for-source-knowledge-graph"></a>

## Entry 14 — 2026-11-02 — docs(feature): behaviours for source knowledge graph

*Kind: product. Status: accepted.*

## Context

The accepted vision in #42 calls for a source-owned graph that grounds AI agents and can support wider views than the ontology alone. A single repository need not contain every fact needed for all C4 levels. The analyst needed to decide which sources may supply evidence, when a changed file blocks the PR check, and whether inferred relationships can be published.

## Decision

Include selected design and architecture documents as evidence alongside code, tests, ontology terms, and eligible deployment files. A changed file inside declared graph coverage requires a graph refresh or an explicit record that review found no fact change; the deterministic pull-request check blocks when that review is missing. Publish inferred relationships only when they are clearly labeled and cite reviewable source observations, and present them as tentative to agents.

## Consequences

Maintainers can review direct assertions, inferences, evidence, and gaps in the same PR. CI can check structure and freshness but cannot establish semantic truth, so maintainers remain responsible for claims. Repositories can declare partial coverage; out-of-scope files do not trigger the freshness check. The recorded revision representation, graph schema, extraction method, and query interface remain for architecture to decide. The numeric grounding target remains deferred until a representative baseline exists.

<a id="entry-docs-feature-architecture-for-source-knowledge-graph"></a>

## Entry 15 — 2026-11-02 — docs(feature): architecture for source knowledge graph

*Kind: product. Status: accepted.*

## Context

The accepted vision and behaviours require source-owned, reviewable facts for AI agent grounding, labeled inferences, explicit gaps, and a blocking PR freshness check within declared coverage. The design must work across C#, TypeScript, Java, and Python, permit selected documents as evidence, use only Terraform for JointBooking deployment evidence, and avoid a required external graph service or Graphify dependency. Adopting repositories already use `ontology.ttl` as the ontology source of truth.

## Decision

Store the graph as canonical Turtle files with named resources and shared ontology concept IRIs. Derive the effective revision from the containing Git commit ([ADR 0005](https://github.com/jamiemitchellconsultants/InternalOntology/blob/feature/source-knowledge-graph/architect/docs/adr/0005-source-graph-git-data.md)). Record reviewed source blob IDs and check changed paths against both base and proposed coverage ([ADR 0006](https://github.com/jamiemitchellconsultants/InternalOntology/blob/feature/source-knowledge-graph/architect/docs/adr/0006-source-graph-freshness.md)). Install an agent protocol, local reader and checker, and read-only workflow through an explicit option ([ADR 0007](https://github.com/jamiemitchellconsultants/InternalOntology/blob/feature/source-knowledge-graph/architect/docs/adr/0007-source-graph-opt-in-runtime.md)). Use a versioned core RDF vocabulary with defined adopter extensions ([ADR 0008](https://github.com/jamiemitchellconsultants/InternalOntology/blob/feature/source-knowledge-graph/architect/docs/adr/0008-source-graph-vocabulary.md)).

## Consequences

A PR exposes changes to assertions, evidence, coverage, and no-fact-change reviews. The deterministic checker validates a documented canonical Turtle subset, structure, and freshness without making semantic claims; maintainers judge whether evidence supports direct or inferred assertions. The source graph can be combined with the canonical ontology by RDF consumers without translating JSON. Repositories can participate with partial coverage, and downstream consumers derive only the views their pinned facts support. The first implementation must define and test the Turtle contract, coverage priority, reader output, and local/CI revision modes. Numeric grounding targets remain deferred until a representative baseline exists.

<a id="entry-docs-feature-plan-source-knowledge-graph-implementation"></a>

## Entry 16 — 2026-11-02 — docs(feature): plan source knowledge graph implementation

*Kind: product. Status: accepted.*

## Context

The accepted architecture fixes the behaviour of the graph but leaves several contract details to the developer: the shape of the graph settings in `OntologyConfig`, the IRIs for evidence roles and outcomes, how a deleted file is recorded, how a review record is named, and how the checker and reader are invoked locally and in CI. The plan has to settle these without changing a behaviour or an ADR, keep the installed scripts byte-identical across repositories, and let every claim be proved by a test that runs without a model, secret or network.

## Decision

Fill the gaps conservatively and record them in the task plan's decisions table. An evidence role with no configured selector accepts no evidence, so Terraform-only deployment is plain configuration. Every existing covered file must carry a review record whose blob equals its current blob; pull request mode adds the base-and-proposed union rule from ADR 0006 and a guard against a pull request disabling or relocating the check. Revisions are read from Git objects, including the index for a staged candidate, never from the working tree. Rejected: baking a fixed evidence default into the scripts, which would break byte-identical installs, and reading configuration from the working directory, which a pull request could rewrite.

## Consequences

The build can proceed task by task with each behaviour mapped to the task that proves it. The first broad declaration of coverage by an adopter needs one review record per covered file, which an agent must write by hand; the checker prints each expected blob ID, and a record-writing helper is left as a possible later change. The branch-protection integration of the new workflow is verified only in a disposable GitHub repository during the final task, or reported as unverified. Numeric grounding targets stay deferred.

## Entry 17 — 2026-11-02 — Clarify Git command delimiters in source graph plan

*Kind: product. Status: accepted.*

## Context

The build found that Task 3 required `-z` for every Git command, although the specified object and tree commands do not all support that option.

## Decision

Use argument arrays for every Git invocation and NUL-delimited output for commands that list paths. Keep the detailed plan's specified arguments for object and tree commands.

## Consequences

The build can handle unusual filenames without adding unsupported options to Git commands. The graph behaviour and architecture remain unchanged.

<a id="entry-clarify-source-graph-configuration-reset-behaviour"></a>

## Entry 18 — 2026-11-02 — Clarify source graph configuration reset behaviour

*Kind: product. Status: accepted.*

## Context

The source graph plan said existing configuration is never edited, while the installer's explicit content reset already replaces adopter-owned configuration. The build needed a consistent rule for combining the graph option with that reset.

## Decision

Preserve existing configuration for normal installs and forced upgrades. An explicit content reset restores the graph-enabled starter configuration and discards the prior settings, consistent with the existing reset contract.

## Consequences

The detailed plan includes a test for the combined options and the absence of a config notice after reset. Existing settings remain protected during normal installation and forced upgrades; an explicit reset remains destructive.

<a id="entry-plan-symlink-safe-source-graph-command-execution"></a>

## Entry 19 — 2026-11-03 — Plan symlink-safe source graph command execution

*Kind: product. Status: accepted.*

## Context

The bare-Git acceptance test found that the installed commands can silently exit without running when their script paths include a symbolic link. The supplied test also allowed the nested shipped-test invocation to run no tests.

## Decision

Task 10 will repair both command entry-point guards and test execution through linked script paths. Its acceptance tests will assert command output and run the installed test files explicitly. Keep the existing task commits intact and include the repairs in the single Task 10 commit.

## Consequences

The build retains its ordered commit history and verifies that both commands actually run from a bare checkout. Script-path resolution does not change where graph data or configuration is read. GitHub branch-protection verification remains a separate acceptance check.

<a id="entry-plan-final-source-graph-review-repairs"></a>

## Entry 20 — 2026-11-03 — Plan final source graph review repairs

*Kind: product. Status: accepted.*

## Context

Final review of the pushed build found that an empty evidence path with line zero produced no findings, graph opt-in beside an existing custom-namespace config wrote starter files in a different namespace, and removing a covered selector with its evidence and assertions escaped the PR check when source files did not change. The architecture requires removed coverage to remain explicitly unknown or excluded with a reason. GitHub branch-protection integration remains unverified.

## Decision

Compare each base covered selector by its literal pattern with proposed coverage declarations. Retain the selector as covered, or retain it as unknown or excluded with a non-empty reason; narrowing uses a reasoned old-scope marker plus a higher-priority covered selector for the retained area. Validate evidence paths and line bounds independently. Generate new starter graph files from a preserved config's namespace during normal opt-in or force; explicit reset replaces config and starters together. Append one Task 11 repair commit to the existing build branch without rewriting its ten task commits.

## Consequences

Coverage removal is visible even without changed source files. Literal pattern comparison avoids guessing glob equivalence from tracked files, so a selector rewrite must retain an explicit old-scope marker. The existing base/head review-record rule still applies to changed files. The installed checker, installer and acceptance tests receive focused regressions. The build handoff remains blocked until the plan amendment is reviewed and merged, the pushback is cleared, and Task 11 passes. Branch-protection integration remains for user acceptance.
